1. The Last Long Vacation
2. A Summer to Remember
3. The Idea
4. Gathering the Memories
5. One More Adventure
6. The Sealing
7. Until Next Time

The Long Vacation is the final story of the Haaraya programme, and a farewell to the children of Tafiya Estate. The whole journey began, many books ago, with a single small word: a. It is only right that it should close, here at the very end, with the word that carries every story onward, and

The long vacation had come at last, the great stretch of holiday that opened ahead like a whole golden country. But this year felt different. Isa was one of the oldest estate children now, and after these holidays he and his friends would start secondary school. Something was ending, though something new was surely beginning too.

image.note: Isa standing at the estate gate in bright morning light, looking down the long empty holiday road ahead; a thoughtful, slightly wistful expression; the familiar estate behind him

pages.text: On the first morning, Isa met Isi, Sani, Hanan and Nosa under the big tree by the gate, just as they had a thousand times before. "This is our last long vacation all together," said Hanan quietly. Nobody spoke for a moment. Then Isa grinned. "Then let's make it the best one anyone's ever had," he said.

image.note: Five friends gathered under the big tree by the gate: Isa grinning, Hanan quiet, the others caught between fondness and a little sadness; dappled sunlight through the leaves

pages.text: They filled the first weeks with everything they loved. They cycled the length of the estate, played long games that ran till Amina's solar lamps blinked on at dusk, and sat in the new heritage library reading until the pages blurred. Yet a small sadness sat underneath the fun. Soon they would all be scattered to different schools.

image.note: The friends playing a lively game on an estate path at dusk as Amina's small solar lamps flicker on around them; warm evening glow; movement and joy with a soft golden light

pages.text: "I wish we could keep this summer somehow," said Isi one evening, watching the sky turn orange. "Not just remember it. Keep it." The friends fell quiet, thinking. And in that quiet, sitting on the library steps where old Miss Adunni's pupils had once sat, an idea began to take shape in Isa's mind.

image.note: The five friends sitting in a row on the heritage library steps at sunset, faces orange in the light; Isi gazing at the sky; Isa's expression sharpening with a dawning idea

pages.text: "A time capsule," Isa announced the next day, eyes shining. "We fill a box with things from right now, from all of us, and we seal it up. Then years and years from now, when we're grown, we open it again together." The friends stared, then broke into wide grins. It was perfect. It was exactly right.

image.note: Isa standing before his four friends, arms wide with excitement, mid-announcement; the others' faces lighting up with delight as the idea lands; the library behind them

pages.text: They found a strong metal box with a tight lid, big enough to hold a whole summer. "But it can't just be us five," said Nosa. "It should be everyone. The whole estate." And so the friends set off, door to door, to invite every child on Tafiya Estate to put something of themselves inside.

image.note: The friends carrying a sturdy metal box between them along an estate path, knocking at a bright modern doorway where other children appear, curious and eager; sunny

pages.text: The memories came pouring in. Amina gave one of her first tiny solar lamps. Itohan wrote the story of how she saved the old house. Boma drew the great storm and the night the neighbours dug out the drain together. Chidera and her London cousin sent a photograph of two dishes side by side. Each gift held a whole tale.

image.note: A table spread with the children's contributions: a small solar lamp, a handwritten story, a bold drawing of a storm, a photo of two dishes; the estate children crowding round adding their gifts

pages.text: Younger children brought drawings and letters to their future selves. Baba Sule, though not a child at all, asked to add one thing: a single page copied gently from Miss Adunni's old ledger, so the past and the present would rest together in the dark of the box, waiting quietly for the future.

image.note: Elderly Baba Sule bending to place a single aged ledger page into the open box among the children's drawings and letters; small children watching solemnly; tender, meaningful

pages.text: Before the sealing, the friends took one last great trip together. A bus carried them out along the winding road to Gurara Falls, where the water thundered down the rocks in a roar of white spray and rainbows hung shimmering in the mist. They stood at the rail, soaked and laughing, shouting to be heard above the falls.

image.note: The five friends at a viewing rail before the mighty Gurara Falls, white water crashing down, rainbows in the mist, all soaked and laughing with arms raised; spectacular and joyful

pages.text: "We have to remember this exact moment," Isa called over the roar. So they crowded together, and a passing traveller took their photograph: five friends, arms flung around one another, grinning like the whole world was theirs. That photograph, still damp at the edges, went straight into the capsule that very night.

image.note: The five friends posed tightly together in front of the falls, arms around one another, huge grins, spray flying; the framing of a treasured photograph being taken

pages.text: On the last evening of the vacation, the whole estate gathered outside the heritage library. Amina's lamps glowed warm along the paths, and the long table was heavy with food. The time capsule sat in the middle of it all, brimming with a summer's worth of memories, waiting for its lid to close on it at last.

image.note: A large warm evening gathering outside the lit heritage library; solar lamps glowing along the paths; a laden table; the open metal capsule at the centre; the whole estate cast present

pages.text: Isa spoke a few words, though his voice went a little unsteady. "This box holds who we are, right now," he said. "One day we'll open it and remember." Then, together, all the children pressed the heavy lid down until it clicked shut. A whole summer was sealed inside.

image.note: All the children's hands pressing the heavy lid onto the capsule together; Isa mid-speech, moved; the crowd watching warmly; near the step a tiny ant sits cross-legged, unbothered as ever, quietly watching the sealing

pages.text: They set the capsule into a snug space in the library wall, behind a small brass door, with a date carved above it many years away. "Until next time," Isa whispered, resting his hand flat against the cool brass. Around him the estate glowed, full of light and voices, the same estate that would still be here when they returned.

image.note: Isa resting his palm against a small closed brass door set in the library wall, a future date carved above it; behind him the glowing, bustling evening gathering; quiet and hopeful

pages.text: The long vacation was over. New schools waited, new friends, new stories none of them could yet imagine. But whatever came, this place and these people would always be theirs to come back to. And as the stars came out over Tafiya Estate, the friends looked up, ready for everything that lay ahead, and

image.note: The five friends standing together looking up at a wide starry sky over the softly lit estate, faces open and hopeful; a wide, quiet, forward-looking closing image; the whole programme's farewell frame
